crime_highlights: four youths, including [I.Z.N.], come running at a high rate of speed from a classroom and attack [Mr. G.] with blows from their fists
The attack is brief but violent
[I.Z.N.] can be observed kicking or stomping [Mr. G.] in the area of his head
rationale_highlights: three of the four youths, including I.Z.N., were of Aboriginal heritage
I.Z.N.'s Aboriginal heritage; the PSRs filed in respect of each offender
note: Heritage listed only in Crown submission; appeal court never states mitigating effect.

crime_highlights: the appellant Annalee Auckland stabbed her common law spouse

He died from blood loss resulting from a stab wound 16 cm deep that entered the front of his chest striking the superior vena cava and a stab wound seven cm deep that punctured the right carotid artery
rationale_highlights: one of the Gladue factors identified in the report was dislocation from her Aboriginal community
Other factors included familial fragmentation, alienation by her mother, sexual abuse from close family members and lack of education and underemployment
He also considered Ms. Auckland's Aboriginal background and the gravity of the offence she had committed
note: Appeal court says background considered but never that it reduced sentence.

introduced into substance abuse as early as age 10, which led to chronic substance abuse that almost killed him
These findings are supported by the evidence and in my view must be given deference
Mr. Sellars' diminished moral culpability in his unique circumstances as an Aboriginal offender
